journey.intro: What tends to change as alcohol-free days add up. Whatever you log, nothing here closes again.
journey.disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. If you drink heavily every day, talk to a doctor before stopping: cutting out alcohol suddenly can be dangerous.

sleep1.title: Sleep gets lighter before it gets better
sleep1.body: Alcohol helps you fall asleep but cuts into dream sleep later in the night. The first nights without it can feel restless while that rebalances.

water1.title: Rehydrating
water1.body: Alcohol makes you lose more water than you take in. After a few days without it, morning thirst and headaches tend to ease.

sleep7.title: Deeper sleep
sleep7.body: After about a week many people take a little longer to fall asleep but wake less during the night and feel more rested in the morning.

stomach14.title: A calmer stomach
stomach14.body: Alcohol irritates the stomach lining and increases acid. Two weeks without it is often enough for heartburn and bloating to settle.

liver30.title: Liver and blood pressure
liver30.body: In studies of regular drinkers who took a month off, liver fat and blood pressure tended to fall. How much depends on how much you drank before.

mind90.title: Mood and focus
mind90.body: Many people report a steadier mood and clearer mornings after a few months. Drinking less can help with that, though it is not a treatment for low mood.
